text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- BANKS BET ON EXPLOSION IN PERSONAL CREDIT

The Central Bank's loosening of credit restrictions has prompted banks to expand portfolios for loans to industry, trade and individuals. A survey shows top financial institutions expect credit transactions to rise by 15 to 25 percent in the second half.
-- FINDING CAUSES TUMULT OVER AMADOR AGUIAR'S INHERITANCE

Cooper's & Lybrand and Price Waterhouse are competing for a $2.0 million contract to determine the true value of the inheritance left by the first wife of Amador Aguiar, the founder of Bradesco. The fortune is estimated at 100 million reais.
-- BANKS ASSUME JOAO SANTOS GROUP DEBT

The Joao Santos group of northeastern Brazil and a group of creditor banks reached an agreement over the group's 500 million real debt, one of the largest debts faced by Brazil's financial system last year.
O GLOBO
-- ACCORD WITH U.S. TO COMBAT ILLEGAL ARMS SALES IN BRAZIL

The Brazilian government plans to sign later this year an agreement with the United States to step up the fight against arms trafficking in this country. The accord calls for U.S. arms merchants to tell authorities who they sell to.
-- POLICE ADMIT THEY ARE UNDERSTAFFED FOR ELECTIONS
Brazil's military police admitted in a report to elections officials that they do not have enough manpower to guarantee safety in next month's municipal elections.
-- SOUTHEAST RAILROAD AUCTION MAY HAVE ONLY ONE BIDDER
The choicest part of Brazil's federal railway network, the Southeast Branch, will be privatized Friday but only one group of investors has assured it will take part in the bidding.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- ASIAN FIRMS BUY AMAZONIAN LOGGING COMPANIES
Asian logging companies have purchased two Brazilian firms that extract wood from the Amazon and are buying land to further exploit the region's lumber resources.
-- SAO PAULO'S DEBT TOTALS 78.92 PCT OF REVENUES
Sao Paulo Mayor Paulo Maluf's successor will inherit a debt that totals 78.92 percent of the municipality's estimated revenue this year.
-- BRAZILIAN LEFT IS IN DECLINE
The Brazilian left has been unable to put forward an alternative to the neoliberalism espoused by the government of President Fernando Henrique Cardoso.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
